To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the recombinant epimerase of spinach, a photosynthetic organism, is an octamer, in contrast to the dimeric forms of the enzyme from other species, and that its 25-kDa subunit size, as deduced from sequence analysis of the spinach gene and electrophoretic analysis of the purified recomabinant enzyme, is about the same as the corresponding sizes in yeast and mammals.
the recombinant epimerase is octameric, that its subunit size is about 25 kD, that the enzyme is not stabilized by ethylenediamine tetraacetate, and that it is not activated by metal cations.

we have achieved, to the best of our knowledge, the heterologous expression in Escherichia coli of the spinach epimerase gene, which is the first time that this gene has been expressed in any organism, and that we have characterized, purified, and identified the recombinant protein as octameric.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first heterologous expression and characterization of a plant enzyme involved in the pentose-phosphate cycle.

the first heterologous expression in Escherichia coli of an enzyme involved in the Calvin cycle, the first high-specific-activity purification and characterization of an epimerase from a higher plant, and the first report of an octameric form of this enzyme.
the first high-level expression and characterization of an epimerase from photosynthetic organisms and the first demonstration of the octameric nature of a D-ribuloses 5-phosphate 2,3-epimerases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in terms of subunit size, quaternary structure, and metal-ion requirement, the spinach epimerase is a unique member of a class of enzymes that is ubiquitous in living organisms.

the spinach epimerase is octameric and that its subunit size and catalytic properties are similar to those of the epimerases from yeast and mammals, but that it differs from the latter in being insensitive to metal ions.
